correctness.rationale: Nonzero rank-one A=uψ uniquely constrains the image line of E and the row line of F. The equations ψ(v)=1, φ(u)=1, φ(v)=1 produce three exact trace cases according to the unique dependent v, while the zero fiber follows from image(F) in ker(E). Counting covers all q and n≥2, including characteristic 2. The eight independently enumerated full-fiber finite-field cases corroborate, but do not replace, this proof.

originality.rationale: A direct full-text comparison with Jain–Leroy arXiv:2407.12231 finds existence/product decompositions, not prescribed-target numbers for two rank-one idempotents. The closest published finite-field counts use a nilpotent rather than a second rank-one idempotent. The result provides a full trace-stratified fiber law for each rank-one target, including zero; the unlocated classical-pair-geometry risk is reported, so priority is claimed only relative to material inspected.
residual_risks: A classical count in the literature of idempotent pair simultaneous-conjugacy classes or projective incidence schemes may algebraically imply this formula.
The Fountain–Lewin 2009 full text and the complete texts of the two published nearby factorization findings were not inspected; source summaries alone cannot exclude stronger statements.
Search retrieval is not an exhaustive novelty proof.

value.rationale: Factorization existence is classical, but multiplicities are a distinct natural invariant of the minimal-rank stratum in matrix semigroups. The exact map-fiber theorem determines every target and is not implied by rank alone: the trace-zero, trace-one, other-trace and zero targets have genuinely different multiplicities. The idempotent-output frequency displays a dimension-two 3/q versus n≥3 2/q transition, motivating future higher-rank comparisons; no downstream theorem is claimed.
